simple.meaning: בָּדַד (bâdad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to divide , i.e. (reflex.) be solitary.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Leviticus, Psalms, Isaiah, Hosea, beginning at Leviticus 13:46. The surrounding contexts include city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּדַד (H909) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּדַד (bâdad) / H909 is traced through Leviticus 13:46, Psalms 102:8, Isaiah 14:31, Hosea 8:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H909. badad I. [ בָּדַד ] verb be separate, isolated (Arabic cause to withdraw ; II. separate, disunite , Gen 11:8 Saad; IV. divide into parts ; x. go alone, act independently ), only Participle בּוֺדֵד Isa 14:31 (of straggler in army), Hosea 8:9 לוֺ בוֺדֵד מֶּרֶא a wild-ass (simile of Ephraim) going alone for itself (i.e. willfully: see below לְ ), Psa 102:8 (of bird sitting solitarily).

occurrences.englishText: All the days in which the plague is in him he shall be unclean. He is unclean. He shall dwell alone. His dwelling shall be outside of the camp.
My enemies reproach me all day.
Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.
For they have gone up to Assyria,
